[LSER.8.6.2] The ordering keeps anomaly-detection patterns
honest. A rule like `where t.state - t.mean > 2 * t.stdev`
reads `t.mean` and `t.stdev` against the historical
distribution, not against a distribution that already includes
the value being checked. Were absorption to happen before firing,
the new sample would contribute to its own threshold,
distorting comparisons — a small effect on heavy-state
backings with many samples, a large effect on small ring
buffers.
